description: Add React Error Boundary around Three.js Canvas to catch silent WebGL crashes, add debug logging, and improve visual prominence of the 3D chart section so rendering issues are diagnosable.
steps: Add a ChartErrorBoundary class component in PnlGraph3D.tsx that catches errors from the Canvas and shows a fallback message
Wrap the Canvas component with the error boundary
Add console.log at the top of PnlGraph3D render for debugging
Improve the 'Not enough data' message to show context (mode, available data)
Add a visible border/background to the 3D chart container so it is impossible to miss
Verify tsc -b and vite build pass
acceptance_criteria: ChartErrorBoundary class component exists and wraps the Canvas
If WebGL/Three.js crashes, a visible fallback message appears instead of silent failure
console.log outputs render info (points count and mode) for debugging
The 3D chart section has a noticeable border/background distinguishing it visually
vite build produces a bundle without errors
findings: Error boundary added as a class component wrapping the Canvas. tsc -b and vite build both pass. The error boundary will catch WebGL context failures and React render errors from Three.js and display a visible message. The console.log will help diagnose whether the component mounts at all. If the user still sees no graph after this fix, it means the conditional render (trade && history) is evaluating to false - meaning either trade or history is null/undefined at render time.
